# Getting Your Service Menu Right — Fast

• **Start with your revenue reality, not your wishes.** Pull your last 3 months of actual sales data. What are members actually buying? What's your highest-margin offer? Build the menu around what's *working*, not what you think should work. This takes 90 minutes, not a strategy offsite.

• **Create TWO separate menus — coaches need the business version (margins, upsells, package architecture), members get the clean, benefits-focused version.** Your coaches won't sell what they don't understand the profit picture on. Frame offerings by outcome ("Build strength in 12 weeks") not features for members; by commission/margin for coaches.

• **Price anchoring: Make your mid-tier package the obvious choice.** If you offer Basic/Standard/Premium, price it so Standard looks 20% better value than Basic and Premium feels like a luxury splurge, not a ripoff. Most gyms price wrong here — test a price increase on Premium first; members rarely choose it anyway.

• **Lock in your "included vs. paid" line ruthlessly.** Every blurry line costs you money. Decide NOW: Is nutrition coaching included in membership or £X extra? Is form check included in group classes? Document it so coaches aren't making it up daily and undercutting your margins.

• **Post it where coaches see it daily** — literally on their phone, in the gym, in your WhatsApp. If they don't know it cold, they won't sell it. Give them 15 minutes to learn it this week, then quiz them.

What's your current highest revenue generator — classes, 1-on-1 coaching, or packages?

## REVENUE TRENDS & ACTIONS

**Revenue momentum is strong but member quality is declining — fix retention immediately.**

- **Revenue up 37% (Jul–Sep: £57,940 vs Apr–Jun: £48,697) but Rev/member down 4% (£139 → £133).** You're adding members (153 vs 121 in Apr) but they're paying less per head. Check: are new joiners on lower-tier plans? Are class packs underselling? Audit your pricing tiers and test a tiered upsell at sign-up (peak class add-on, nutrition plan, PT sessions at £15–25/head).

- **Churn spiked to 12.8% in May, then stabilised at 5.6–6.2%.** September's 6.2% is acceptable but *not* improving. Target: drop to <4% within 90 days via (a) automated retention email at day 14 (low-attendance members), (b) monthly member feedback survey to catch pain points, (c) "at-risk" class for members logging <2 visits/month.

- **Sep revenue £22,016 is your peak — replicate that.** What drove it? (Summer body push? Referral surge? New class schedule?) Isolate the variable and repeat. If it was July launch marketing, plan Sep 2026 campaign now (same budget, same channels).

- **Fill quiet classes with off-peak pricing.** Sept saw 166 members but revenue only grew 37%. Offer £5 discount for 6am or 2pm sessions (lowest-utilisation slots) to flatten demand and lock in frequency. Target: 10% uplift in class attendance, +£800–1,200/month revenue.

---

## EXPENSE TRENDS & REDUCTIONS

**Without full P&L, assume staffing & rent are your two largest line items (post-relocation in Apr). Two moves:**

- **Rent vs revenue ratio check:** Post-relocation (larger space), you need to confirm rent didn't grow faster than revenue. Sep revenue £22k on ~166 members = £132/member. If new rent >35% of revenue, the studio is too big or pricing too low. If rent is now £6,500+/month, you need £18,500+ revenue baseline just to cover it — you're at £22k but margins are tight. Benchmark: women's gyms typically run 25–30% occupancy cost. Get the lease reviewed if rent >£7,000.
